record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ···. Must the next multiplicity-cluster sums also be bounded by their ball values, namely λ₄ + λ₅ over λ₁ in dimension 2 and, in general dimension n, (λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})/λ₁ ≤ ((n−1)(n+2)/2) · j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}²?

evidence.quote: It may also be true that in two dimensions (λ₄ + λ₅)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₄ + λ₅)/λ₁)|disk = 2j²_{2,1}/j²_{0,1} ≈ 9.121 and in general dimension n (λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})/λ₁ ≤ ((n−1)(n+2)/2) j²_{p+2,1}/j²_{p,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
$$0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le \lambda_2(\Omega)\le \lambda_3(\Omega)\le\cdots$$
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicities) of the Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, i.e. of the problem
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$
For an integer $m\ge 0$ and positive integer $k$, let $j_{m,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_m$. For a ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, the Dirichlet eigenvalues are known explicitly in terms of zeros of Bessel functions $J_{p+\ell}$ with $p=(n-2)/2$, and one has in particular that $\lambda_1(B)$ corresponds to $j_{p,1}^2/R^2$ (where $R$ is the radius), while the next eigenvalue cluster involves $j_{p+1,1}^2/R^2$, and the subsequent cluster involves $j_{p+2,1}^2/R^2$.

On a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the first eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ is simple, the next cluster $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{n+1}$ consists of $n$ equal eigenvalues, and the following cluster $\lambda_{n+2},\dots,\lambda_{n(n+3)/2}$ consists of $\tfrac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}$ equal eigenvalues. In particular, for a disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ ($n=2$, $p=0$),
$$\frac{\lambda_4(B)+\lambda_5(B)}{\lambda_1(B)}=\frac{2\,j_{2,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2}\approx 9.121.$$

Prove or disprove the following conjectured isoperimetric inequalities for arbitrary bounded domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$:

(a) In dimension $n=2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_4(\Omega)+\lambda_5(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)}\le \frac{2\,j_{2,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2}.$$

(b) In general dimension $n\ge 2$, writing $p=(n-2)/2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{n+2}(\Omega)+\lambda_{n+3}(\Omega)+\cdots+\lambda_{n(n+3)/2}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)}\le \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}{2}\cdot\frac{j_{p+2,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2},$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjectured cluster-sum bounds for higher Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian (extending Ashbaugh–Benguria-type ratios beyond $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ and $(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1})/\lambda_1$) appear to remain open. Recent literature on Ashbaugh–Benguria-style conjectures addresses lower-order eigenvalues (e.g., $(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1})/\lambda_1$), but no proof of the $\lambda_4+\lambda_5$ cluster bound in 2D or its $n$-dimensional generalization was located.

status_evidence.title: On Ashbaugh-Benguria's Conjecture about Lower Order Dirichlet Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Work on the conjecture for the sum (lambda_2+...+lambda_{n+1})/lambda_1, the previous cluster.
status_evidence.claim: Research focuses on the immediately preceding cluster, indicating the next cluster bound remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on Laplacian eigenvalues including conjectured ball-extremal bounds for eigenvalue ratios.
status_evidence.claim: The cluster-sum conjectures are stated as open problems.
